# `∘` — Atop

Dyadic operator. Keys: `Alt-t`. Hanzi: `承`

`f∘g Y` is `f(g Y)`, and `X f∘g Y` is `f(X g Y)`.

```bpl
2 -∘+ 3            ⍝ ¯5
```
See [Rank](jot-diaeresis.qmd) for applying a function to cells of a chosen rank.

## Before an operator

`∘` before an operator finishes the current run as its left operand. `⊂⊢∘⌸` is `(⊂⊢)⌸`; `+/÷≢∘⍤1` applies the mean train at rank 1. Named operators have the same behavior. Spaces or parentheses keep any earlier function or left argument outside the run.

```bpl
m←2 3ρι6 ◇ +/÷≢∘⍤1m   ⍝ 1 4
```

Before a function, `∘` still means Atop. [Composing functions](../composition.qmd#operators-on-trains) describes both uses.

## Inverse

`(f∘g)⁻Y` is `g⁻ f⁻ Y`. `X(f∘g)⁻Y` is `X g⁻ f⁻ Y`.

```bpl
(-∘÷)⁻¯0.5   ⍝ 2
```
